item.title: bj-4: console sanity and quality runs tabs; measured elapsed and dev identity in the sanity ledger

results.statement: Every time atm-bd prints for a person (console header, rows, PR sheet, Diagnostics view, cron digest) is 24-hour local time produced by the program's one display formatter; every time it writes to a file or log is UTC ISO-8601 with a Z suffix.

results.statement: atm-bd must show a sanity runs page and a quality runs page, newest run on top, one line per run; the sanity line must carry a pass/fail column and an elapsed-time column for JEV and for LLM each, and a column with the name and nerd icon of the dev whose work was checked; elapsed comes from the Jev client's own return and from a timer fenced around the LLM subagent, and the same rows feed the OTel database in the next atm release.
results.quote: sanity agent never does it and I always need to ask.  it is the only thing I want to see from sanity agent.  perhaps we should consider adding a tui page for both sanity and quality which showed the runs sorted by most recent (on top).  the sanity page would have 1 line per run and both jev + llm would have columns for pass/fail AND elapsed time (which is currently not calculated properly).  Regarding calculation, can't this be returned from the jev.py method call and a timer fencing around the llm agent?  I would also like to have a column for what dev (name and nerd icon) did the work under review.  This would remove the agent distraction and show the data I want to see (and get into otel db on next atm release).
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18 (third round): Rand on the sanity runs table, Jev/LLM failures and refusal ceremony
results.deterministic_check: the console has a sanity page and a quality page; a ledger row has jev_elapsed_s, llm_elapsed_s and dev fields; jev_client.py returns elapsed; the dev-sanity prompt wraps the LLM spawn in a start/end time; the sanity reply template no longer renders the runs table
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: A Jev or LLM call failure must be retried up to three times before the slot reports failure; the failure reason must appear in the runs page severity table with an icon distinct from a JEV verdict that the work is not done; and no workflow class bead, outage bead, hold on re-dispatch, refusal citation or checker-defect side channel may exist in the sanity or refusal flows.
results.quote: this entire process of hold on re-dispatch sounds like a team trying to manage a reliable asset by making excuses not to deal with failures to call the agent properly.  (I suspect that a subagent sends too much context and jev returns error, instead of editing context, failure is returned.  There are occasionally LLM call fails during heavy traffic times which can be retried 3x before saying fail. )  Make sure that LLM failure reason shows up in severity table in tui AND the fail icon for typesafe API issue is distinctly different from jev answered 'all work NOT done'.  this `Class-bead append and citation on every refusal, and the checker-defect side channel.` also sounds like ceremony I did not know about or approve.
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18 (third round): Rand on the sanity runs table, Jev/LLM failures and refusal ceremony
results.deterministic_check: grep the agents and requirements for 'class bead', 'outage' bead and 'cite' in refusal steps returns nothing; jev_client.py retries three times on a transport error; the console maps kind API_FAILURE to a different icon than verdict FAIL
results.explanation: The directive is carried forward.

results.statement: The GitHub poll interval of atm-bd defaults to 10 minutes and is configurable in the repository configuration and on the command line; one refresh fetches up to 100 PRs per GraphQL page with few fields and pages past 100 rather than dropping PRs.

results.statement: Before each GitHub refresh atm-bd reads the live remaining quota for the resource its mode uses (graphql or core) via gh api rate_limit; when remaining is below the configured threshold (default 50 percent of the limit) it skips the refresh, keeps cached PR data, shows a paused status with the numbers and the local reset time, and refuses forced refreshes until the quota is back above the threshold.
results.quote: can you file another feature request to add the poll interval AND token budget(s) for gh? it should also stop polling if token drop below a threshold (start w/ 50%)
results.context: console lockdown 2026-10-18: Rand's rulings on beads atm-phase-bi.7/.9/.10/.12/.13, ADR-065/066/067
results.deterministic_check: a stubbed rate_limit at 49 percent skips the refresh and shows the pause line with a local reset time; at 51 percent after reset the refresh runs
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.statement: When a dev or fix bead closes, the group's sanity bead must be assigned to the dev-sanity member with the sanity template and vars without any lead action: by the dev's close hook in the same shell command as bd close, and by atm-bd when bd ready lists the sanity bead with no ATM task.
results.quote: the first issue to solve is mechanical.  when dev or fix bd is closed, sanity 'bd ready' is true.  the atm-bd cron/console will 'atm task assign <bead-id> <sanity-agent> --template <template> --args <vars> automatically.  This assignment must be done --as <phase-lead>
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: close a dev bead through the hook in a scratch repo and read atm task list: the sanity task exists before the hook exits; kill the hook between its commands and one atm-bd tick assigns it
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.statement: When a sanity bead closes with PASS, the sanity close hook must assign the group's qa bead to the quality-mgr member with the qa template and vars as the phase lead, with no lead action.
results.quote: likewise, when a sanity-bd passes, the same task assignment occurs 'atm task assign <quality-agent> --template <qa-template> --args <vars> --as <phase-lead>
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: run the sanity role with verdict PASS in a scratch repo and read atm task list: the qa task exists, assigned by the lead identity, before the hook exits
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.statement: atm-task-close.py must switch on a mandatory --role argument, and for the dev and fix roles must check only that a PR exists on pr_target, that the pushed head is the PR head and that origin/<pr_target> is an ancestor of it; it must not check any other layer of the stack or run lint or tests.
results.quote: there should be a switch on role, then depending on role, this will verify that the pr is created, that it is stacked on the layer below (I think this can be determined locally by verifying the base is the previous top of stack).  The checks should be minimal to insure rebase occurred, maintaining the entire stack is NOT dev agents responsibility.  We can not create conditions that it is impossible for the dev agent to complete due to unnecessary python complexity.
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: the dev-role check list in the script source has exactly the PR-exists, head-equals and ancestor checks; a scratch stack whose lower layer is misaligned still passes a correctly based top layer
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.statement: The ATM task of a dev or fix bead must stay open after the dev's close hook runs and must be closed only by the sanity close hook on PASS, as the lead; the dev waits for that close or for the sanity-fail message and starts no other task meanwhile.
results.quote: I would NOT close the atm task until AFTER sanity is green.  This simplifies the dev<->sanity loop.  in the atm-task-close hook for sanity, if sanity pass, THEN atm task is closed (and dev can begin on next task in the queue), sanity task is closed
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: grep atm-task-close.py: no atm task close completed in the dev or fix role; the sanity PASS branch closes the checked bead's task with the lead identity; atm task events of a dev task show the close after the sanity PASS
results.explanation: The anchor does not govern this bead.

results.statement: On a sanity FAIL below the round cap, the sanity close hook must reopen the checked bead to its assignee and send that dev the sanity-fail.xml.j2 template naming each undone deliverable, on the dev's still-open task; it must not create finding beads, a new layer or a new task.
results.quote: If sanity fails, dev bead is re-opened and 'atm send <dev-agent> --template <sanity-rejected-template>'
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
